Safer Claude and Codex identities, fresh sessions when subscriptions change, and tighter protection for credentials and requests. This release also adds model-aware client setup, scoped quota handling and optional Claude usage-window starters.

## Changes

- **Account-bound provider identities.** Claude OAuth requests use the selected subscription's account and device identity, with matching session metadata in the headers and body. Codex preserves valid CLI, Desktop and custom app attribution while binding authentication and session identity to the selected account. Recognition alone grants no identity-learning permission.
- **Fresh sessions on subscription switches.** Each conversation gets a provider session for its current subscription. Switching A → B → A creates three different provider sessions. Inactivity expires a session after 30 minutes by default (`provider-session-idle-seconds`); available conversation history and tool state continue, and prompt-cache keys remain separate. Ordinary token refresh preserves sessions and healthy connections.
- **Safer outbound traffic.** Provider header policies filter private credentials, proxy attribution and hop-by-hop headers for every caller. Upstream HTTP clients refuse redirects, and OAuth failures expose safe classifications instead of raw endpoint response bodies or transport details. Subscription connection pools and TLS resumption state are isolated by account. Account replacement cannot be overwritten by a stale refresh.
- **Trusted identity learning.** Only authenticated named clients with `trust-client-identity: true` can teach shared Claude/Codex identities. Learned versions and runtime profiles are validated, record provenance and can be inspected or reset from Config or the management API. Legacy profiles without trusted provenance are ignored.
- **Codex HTTP/WebSocket parity.** Preserve residency requirements and supported reasoning-summary stream options, apply safe configured headers on both transports, and use the same identity policy for subscription image and compaction requests. Routes unable to honor a requested residency constraint are rejected explicitly. Native prompt-cache-key omission remains intact.
- **Scoped quotas and model-aware setup.** Model-specific limits pause the affected models rather than unrelated work. Model setup uses the selected model's capabilities for client configuration, with matching named-client model restrictions. Used-up windows show their reset time, and temporary upstream account errors clear automatically when their deadline passes.
- **Optional Claude window starters.** Start inactive five-hour usage windows automatically, always or during selected working hours, with a manual Start now action on supported accounts. This is off by default. Each starter makes a small real request and consumes subscription quota; it does not increase weekly allowance. Attempts survive restarts and share locking with banked resets.
- **Refreshed client compatibility.** Updated bundled client identities and documented reviews for Claude Code, Codex, Grok Build, Muse Code, Devin CLI and Antigravity, with regression coverage for native metadata and cache-key behavior.

## Upgrading

- From v0.8.1, the usage database stays on schema 5; this release introduces no usage-schema migration. Continue taking consistent backups before upgrades.
- Identity learning is now opt-in for each named client. Enable **Trust client identity** only for clients allowed to update the shared emulation profile; shared API keys and open access cannot teach identities.
- Inbound headers outside the provider policy are consumed locally. Add required safe extension names under `upstream-header-allowlist`; invalid or protected configured header names fail validation. Intentional gateway credentials remain supported on API-key and custom-provider routes.
- Upstream redirects are no longer followed. Configure the final endpoint URL for any custom service that previously redirected requests.
- Restart starts fresh provider sessions. Native application context, credentials, request content, egress IP and connection characteristics remain visible to providers; preserving or emulating client identities does not provide invisibility.

See [provider identity and sessions](https://github.com/DigitalPals/Fusebox/blob/v0.9.0/docs/provider-identity.md), [window starters](https://github.com/DigitalPals/Fusebox/blob/v0.9.0/docs/window-starters.md) and [compatibility reviews](https://github.com/DigitalPals/Fusebox/blob/v0.9.0/docs/client-compatibility.md) for configuration and limits.
